observations.body: Moses recalls forty days, divine writing, the calf, broken tablets, repeated fasting, threatened destruction, prayer for Aaron, and appeals to promise and reputation.
observations.label: Moses retells the calf, broken tablets, and intercession

observations.body: Moses retells the calf, broken tablets, and intercession belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Deuteronomy 9:7–29 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 9:7–29 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Moses retells the calf, broken tablets, and intercession belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
